### Interactive lecture -- What makes a good theory? How do we make a theory good: watch this to get started on learning and thinking about what what theories are and do, and how we can think critically about them {#sec-7143-w3-lectures-lecture} 

You can watch the lecture for the video using the video playback windows shown next. The lecture is broken into five parts, each about 10-20 minutes long.

1. **We need to talk about theory**
2. **What theories are and do**
3. **Why talking about this stuff is useful**
4. **How we can build or develop theories**
5. **What Makes a Good Theory, and How Do We Make a Theory Good?**

::: callout-tip
During the lecture, I suggest some questions you can think about. Reflecting on your responses to these questions will help you to learn.
:::

You can download the lecture slides as a .html file you can open in any browser.

The slides end with a references list but don't worry about reading what's in the references list, we give you recommended readings in @sec-7143-w3-reading.

::: callout-tip
The slides presented in the next videos can be downloaded as a web page: `doing-theory-good.html.` 

- [Lecture slides](files/doing-theory-good.html)

When you download the file, double click on it to open it in your usual web browser for viewing.
:::

Next, you can see the lecture elements. We recommend that you watch them in sequence.

1. **We need to talk about theory** (~7 minutes). Why we need to talk about theories. Why this will be useful, for life, for students. How we will do this.

3. **Why talking about this stuff is useful** (~19 minutes). Why are we bothering to think or talk about this stuff? Isn’t it obvious? Is it worth the effort? ## Reading {#sec-7143-w3-reading}

::: {.callout-tip title="Easy access to readings"}
All reading is accessible via the library.

- **Essential**: We expect you to be familiar with these reading. You will be assessed on this.
- **Recommended**: We highly recommend these readings. They often provide a different perspective, or explain things in a different way.
- **Optional**: Further readings for those interested.
:::

This week, the reading is optional but **Recommended**:

- Guest, O. (2024). What Makes a Good Theory, and How Do We Make a Theory Good? Computational Brain & Behavior, 7, 508–522. <https://doi.org/10.1007/s42113-023-00193-2> **Recommended**
- van Rooij, I. (2022). Psychological models and their distractors. Nature Reviews Psychology, 1(3), 127–128. <https://doi.org/10.1038/s44159-022-00031-5> **Recommended**
